sources.title: Helix 2.5

paragraphs.text: Today we are introducing Helix 2.5, the most advanced neural network Figure has built.
paragraphs.locator: HTML paragraph immediately after title/byline.

paragraphs.text: Helix 02 showed that a neural policy could coordinate a humanoid's whole body over long horizons, from unloading a dishwasher to running a logistics task autonomously for 200 hours. But those systems learned from data collected where the robots would operate.
paragraphs.locator: Next consecutive HTML paragraph.

paragraphs.text: Helix 2.5 was built to answer a harder question: can a humanoid enter a home it has never seen and immediately get to work, with its whole body, on its own?
paragraphs.locator: Next consecutive HTML paragraph.

paragraphs.text: To find out, we pretrained Helix 2.5 on Index, Figure's global-scale dataset of human behavior. From that single foundation model, we produced three behaviors: tidying living rooms, folding towels, and making beds. Then we took the robot into 30 Bay Area homes with zero data collected in any of them.
paragraphs.locator: Next consecutive HTML paragraph.

assets.caption: Figure 1: Zero-Shot Success in 30 Homes: Success rates of models trained from scratch vs. models trained with Index. Index accounts for the majority of Helix 2.5's zero-shot capability.
Table 1: Evaluation Task Definitions and Setup

sources.title: S1

paragraphs.text: One year ago, we released an in-context learner for locomotion that adapts by accumulating live experience in its prompt (Liu et al., 2025). Today we are sharing manipulation results from our flagship robotic foundation model S1, built from the ground up as an in-context learner. Show it a video of a task, short or long, seen or unseen, and it executes.
paragraphs.locator: Paragraph under h2 “S1: An In-Context Learner”; citation was omitted from the proposed version.

paragraphs.text: This post is the first in a series we will release over the coming months; today's focus is on analyzing the in-context learning capabilities of S1, and future posts will go into depth on how S1 is trained.
paragraphs.locator: Next paragraph under same h2.

Training conditions are held fixed.'; Fig. 7 'Success rate against the number of post-training demonstrations on a new unseen task. The in-context learning policy is flat because it never trains — it is given one demonstration in its prompt. sources.title: GEN-1.5

paragraphs.text: Humans have a remarkable ability to perform new physical skills from only one or a few examples. Our latest robot foundation model, GEN-1.5, exhibits the beginnings of that same ability: it can learn a new task in seconds, from a single example, without gradient updates or fine-tuning. It displays broad capabilities across one-shot and few-shot learning from demonstration, as well as zero-shot physical generalization. Although the tasks are simple and short-horizon, this is the first model we know for which one-shot and few-shot learning of physical skills have emerged at scale. We view these results as a significant step towards our mission of building general intelligence for the physical world.

sources.title: Rho-alpha

paragraphs.text: Today, we are announcing Rho-alpha (ρα), our first robotics model derived from Microsoft’s Phi series of vision-language models.
paragraphs.locator: Paragraph after article introduction. HTML uses ρα and the Phi-series link has hidden sr-only text “(opens in new tab)”; the visible page text excludes that helper.

paragraphs.text: We invite organizations interested in evaluating Rho-alpha for their robots and use cases to express interest in the Rho-alpha Research Early Access Program. Rho-alpha will also be made available via Microsoft Foundry at a later date.
paragraphs.locator: Next visible paragraph; an inline hidden “(opens in new tab)” follows the link in source HTML.

paragraphs.text: Rho-alpha translates natural language commands into control signals for robotic systems performing bimanual manipulation tasks. It can be described as a VLA+ model in that it expands the set of perceptual and learning modalities beyond those typically used by VLAs. For perception, Rho-alpha adds tactile sensing, with efforts underway to accommodate modalities such as force. For learning, we are working toward enabling Rho-alpha to continually improve during deployment by learning from feedback provided by people.
paragraphs.locator: Next visible paragraph, full paragraph; the proposal had only its first four sentences.

sources.title: Step 3.7 Flash

paragraphs.text: Step 3.7 Flash is a 198B-parameter sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) vision-language model that combines a 196B-parameter language backbone with a 1.8B-parameter vision encoder for native image understanding. Engineered for high-frequency production workloads, it activates approximately 11B parameters per token and delivers a throughput of up to 400 tokens per second. Step 3.7 Flash supports a 256k context window and offers three selectable reasoning levels (low, medium, and high) so developers can easily balance speed, cost, and cognitive depth.
paragraphs.locator: heading id introduction; following two p elements

paragraphs.text: We built Step 3.7 Flash for developers who need to scale agentic workflows that combine perception, search, and reasoning. It is designed to handle intensive tasks such as parsing massive financial reports in one pass, running multi-step search loops with cross-source verification, or operating concurrent coding agents in high-throughput pipelines.
paragraphs.locator: heading id introduction; following two p elements

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3.5

paragraphs.text: Mistral Medium 3.5 is our first flagship merged model. It is a dense 128B model with a 256k context window, handling instruction-following, reasoning, and coding in a single set of weights. Mistral Medium 3.5 replaces its predecessor Mistral Medium 3.1 and Magistral in Le Chat. It also replaces Devstral 2 in our coding agent Vibe. sources.title: Nova 2.5 Sonic

paragraphs.text: Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic is designed for enterprise use cases, unifying speech understanding and generation capabilities to enable human-like voice conversations with artificial intelligence (AI) applications. Customers can use Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic for tasks such as customer service call automation, education and language learning, and conversational AI agents across a broad range of industries, including travel, telecommunications, entertainment, and more. This AI Service Card applies to the use of Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic via Amazon Bedrock bidirectional streaming API and Amazon Bedrock Console playground. Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic is a managed sub-service of Amazon Bedrock; customers can focus on executing prompts without having to provision or manage any infrastructure such as instance types, network topology, and endpoint. Not all of the content in the service card is applicable to models hosted on https://nova.amazon.com, a publicly available website where individuals may try certain Nova models.

sources.title: Hy4-preview

paragraphs.text: Hy4 preview is a new-generation Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) flagship model developed by the Tencent Hy Team. The model comprises 770B total parameters, of which 49B are activated per token. The backbone consists of 78 layers, where the first layer uses a standard dense FFN and the remaining 77 layers replace it with MoE, each containing 256 routed experts and 1 shared expert; every token activates the top-8 routed experts along with the shared expert. In addition to the backbone, 1 native MTP layer (10B total parameters, 0.7B activated) is built in for speculative decoding.
paragraphs.locator: First HTML p under h2 'Model Introduction'.

paragraphs.text: On the architecture side, inspired by DeepSeek and GLM, the attention module employs Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention (Gated DSA) with IndexCache for cross-layer sparse index reuse. The residual pathway uses iHC (identity Hyper-Connections) to expand inter-layer information flow.
paragraphs.locator: Second consecutive HTML p under h2 'Model Introduction'.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-Max

paragraphs.text: A 2.4-trillion-parameter MoE flagship model with improved capabilities in coding and office scenarios, suitable for professional tasks such as law, finance, and design. It provides native visual understanding, supports semantic parsing of ultra-long documents and long videos, and supports autonomous planning and iteration for long-horizon tasks.
paragraphs.locator: H1 qwen3.8-max → immediately following first paragraph; next paragraphs identify the API model ID and current snapshot.

lineage_evidence.source_type: official Qwen Hugging Face model repository / README HTML capture (open checkpoint documentation, not an API model card)
lineage_evidence.exact_publisher_text: In particular, Qwen3.8-Max is the official version based on Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B with more features, such as vision input & non-thinking support, 1M context length by default, official built-in tools, etc.
lineage_evidence.dom_locator: Visible README blockquote following note that repository contains post-trained weights/configuration and before Qwen3.8 family introduction.
lineage_evidence.boundary: This explicitly establishes that Qwen3.8-Max is the official version based on Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B and adds vision input, non-thinking support, default 1M context and built-in tools. The repository separately describes itself as a text-only post-trained checkpoint requiring thinking mode. It does not claim the API snapshot qwen3.8-max-0902 has weights identical to the repository checkpoint.

snapshot_revision_evidence.source_type: official Alibaba Cloud Model Studio model documentation page
snapshot_revision_evidence.exact_publisher_text: Qwen3.8-Max-0902 (alias qwen3.8-max-2026-09-02) is an upgraded snapshot of qwen3.8-max. Coding capability breaks new ground, handling more complex engineering-scale projects and long-horizon autonomous development. Collaborative agent performance is significantly enhanced, with greater composure in multi-tool orchestration and end-to-end task delivery. Native vision understanding is refined across chart reasoning, document parsing, and multimodal perception — sharper and more reliable. Retains the 1M context window, thinking mode, and full tool ecosystem, evolving at a higher level of intelligence.
